articles.title: Deep Dive into Next.js 16 App Router Caching
articles.body: The App Router fundamentally redesigns how server rendering and caching interact. Instead of rebuilding entire pages or serving purely dynamic responses on every hit, fine-grained tagged caching allows high-concurrency content consoles to scale efficiently. Reads are cached with tags, and writes invalidate only the specific tags affected.

articles.title: High-Throughput Tag-Based Invalidation Strategies
articles.body: In modern content delivery networks and edge-rendering setups, tag-based cache invalidation (revalidateTag) guarantees that readers receive instant updates without triggering a full rebuild of the website or flushing unrelated cache entries.

articles.title: Streaming React Server Components with Suspense
articles.body: When pages contain slow third-party integrations, comments, or analytics panels, streaming enables the core article to render and be readable in milliseconds while secondary panels resolve asynchronously over the wire.

comments.author: Sarah Chen (Staff Engineer)
comments.content: Tagged invalidation with unstable_cache solved our stale-data problem across all edge nodes!

comments.author: Alex Rivera (SRE)
comments.content: The ability to stream slow panels while keeping core text instantly readable is a game changer for perceived performance.

comments.author: Marcus Vance
comments.content: Great breakdown. Tagging by entity slug and collection prevents entire site purges.
